## Description:

Validates date and time values as being appropriately formatted for the ecobee API. 

Adds a restriction on vacation_name (max length of 12 characters was revealed in testing, but is not disclosed in ecobee API documentations).

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #26953 
**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** N/A

## Example entry for `configuration.yaml` (if applicable):
N/A

## Checklist:
  - [x] The code change is tested and works locally.
  - [x] Local tests pass with `tox`. **Your PR cannot be merged unless tests pass**
  - [x] There is no commented out code in this PR.
  - [x] I have followed the [development checklist][dev-checklist]

If user exposed functionality or configuration variables are added/changed:
  - [ ] Documentation added/updated in [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io)

If the code communicates with devices, web services, or third-party tools:
  - [x] [_The manifest file_][manifest-docs] has all fields filled out correctly. Update and include derived files by running `python3 -m script.hassfest`.
  - [x] New or updated dependencies have been added to `requirements_all.txt` by running `python3 -m script.gen_requirements_all`.

If the code does not interact with devices:

**Home Assistant release with the issue:**

-->
.100 dev

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**
N/A

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**

-->
Docker
**Component/platform:**
<!--
Please add the link to the documentation at https://www.home-assistant.io/components/ of the component/platform in question.
-->
Ecobee

**Description of problem:**
Doesn't create a vacation hold (see error)


**Problem-relevant `configuration.yaml` entries and (fill out even if it seems unimportant):**
```yaml

```

**Traceback (if applicable):**
```
2019-09-27 07:22:49 INFO (SyncWorker_5) [pyecobee] Error fetching data from Ecobee while attempting to create vacation hold: {'status': {'code': 7, 'message': 'Validation error. [Rule string(12) failed on: Test Vacation /thermostat/program/calendarEvents/calendarEvent[2]/name]'}}
```

**Additional information:**

@marthoc sorry to keep bugging you.

PR that added: https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/26923
comments: What data are you calling the service with? Looks like it doesn’t like the name you used. Looks like the string may have been over 12 characters and that’s what it didn’t like? The API docs don’t disclose a limit. I’ll need to add more validation. Please confirm.

Huh.  that might be it.  I had one vacation named "Vacation Test" that did not work, but "Italy" worked just fine.  Here was my call that raised the error:

{
  "entity_id": "climate.dining_room",
  "vacation_name": "Vacation Test",
  "cool_temp": 80,
  "heat_temp": 62,
  "start_date": "2019-09-27",
  "start_time": "09:00:00",
  "end_date": "2019-09-28",
  "end_time": "20:00:00"
}
Could be the space also. I will test and then open a PR.
Confirmed that there is a 12 character limit; spaces are allowed. Will patch.

Yep, I just tested it too.  Interesting there's a character limit (and that it's not documented).

Also, just a heads up, spotting an error in the log that there's an error attempting to get thermostat data.  Can open a new issue if you'd prefer.

2019-09-27 09:52:25 INFO (SyncWorker_10) [pyecobee] Error connecting to Ecobee while attempting to get thermostat data.

> Also, just a heads up, spotting an error in the log that there's an error attempting to get thermostat data. Can open a new issue if you'd prefer.
> 
> 2019-09-27 09:52:25 INFO (SyncWorker_10) [pyecobee] Error connecting to Ecobee while attempting to get thermostat data.

Unless it happens repeatedly and your thermostats won't update, that is a normal and expected Error - just means that the particular API request either failed or timed out.
It's...repeating a lot.  Not popping up in my frontend log so it's not a huge deal.  Will check to see if things update later today.  Much appreciated for all your help!
Not sure that that error is related to the recent PRs anyway as nothing about the update calls in pyecobee has changed... but if it doesn't improve then open an Issue and I will investigate.

hmmm....so my log was getting filled with those errors and sensors weren't updating.  Rebooted and haven't gotten an error since.  Tried a bad call with the create_vacation service (as that's the only thing I could think of that triggered the error) and....still updating.  Weird.  I'll keep an eye on it.

Nope, as soon as I posted that it appears to have stopped updating the sensors (no updates in 3 hours on any sensor) and log is full every ~3 minutes with the above error.  I think i recall at one point seeing an error about having to refresh the token but I didn't copy it :-(

Ok please open a new issue. I will need you to test - let things run for a while without calling the service. Any problems? Then call the service and mark when the problems occur, then I need any and all log output. Would help for you enable debug logging for the ecobee component and pyecoee.
